critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now ~1133 lines mixing auth+sync+queries+phase_summary+LLM+backup scheduler+download; the CSV backup section (~lines 1016-1086) should be extracted to /app/backend/backups.py for testability and to keep server.py under 700 lines.

GET /api/backups/{date}/download?token=<jwt> accepts token via query string without checking role — anyone with a valid JWT (viewer included) can download the full Master CSV of any historical date. If backups are considered sensitive, gate with require_admin (or at minimum, log downloads to the audit trail).

backup_now() stores the entire CSV inline in MongoDB (doc['csv']); at ~333 rows/30 cols this is fine (~50KB), but growth to multi-day retention with wider sheets could exceed the 16MB BSON limit. Consider storing gz-compressed or on disk/S3 with only metadata in Mongo.

backup_scheduler() computes the next 04:00 IST wake-up but there is no jitter or retry-on-failure; if the Sheets read errors at 04:00 the day's backup is silently missing until next boot (backup_now runs on startup only if today's is absent).

Download endpoint decodes JWT but never checks token expiry claim explicitly beyond InvalidTokenError; jwt.decode does verify exp by default only when 'exp' in options — confirm JWT_ALG/options enforce exp so stale tokens can't download indefinitely.

Login page 'Quick Login' buttons ship real admin/viewer credentials into the client bundle; acceptable for a demo/preview deploy but should be gated behind an env flag (e.g., REACT_APP_ENABLE_QUICK_LOGIN) before any production release.

Prior comments still open: CORS allow_credentials=True with '*' fallback; POST /api/pods/{name}/analyze open to viewer with no rate-limit; blocker_analyses cache not auto-invalidated on revision bump.
